lyrics:
[Intro: a doorbell note repeating, becoming a single piano note]

[Verse 1: breathy, close, piano only]
I signed the lease on Tuesday
Top floor, the one with the light
Like we said, with the window seat
And the kitchen painted white
I carried up the boxes
I counted every stair
I said "we're home" to no one
Out of habit, to the air

[Chorus: fuller voice, soft kick, pads]
And I got the keys
Two of them, on a ring
One's still warm from the cutting
It doesn't open anything
I walk from room to room
Saying "this is where you'd be"
I got the keys
Nobody told the keys

[Verse 2: breathy, a little bitter]
I guess you're in the suburbs
With someone who can park
Someone who likes the quiet
And is frightened of the dark
I hope the fence is perfect
I hope the lawn is green
I've got a view of rooftops
And a couch you've never seen

[Chorus: fuller voice, handclaps, pads]
And I got the keys
Two of them, on a ring
One's still warm from the cutting
It doesn't open anything
I walk from room to room
Saying "this is where you'd be"
I got the keys
Nobody told the keys

[Bridge: stacked voices building, drums crash in, belted]
Empty boxes, your handwriting
"Kitchen," "books" and "fragile things"
I keep hearing the buzzer ring
I keep running to let you in
And it's the wind, it's the wind, it's the wind

[Final Chorus: quiet again, piano and one voice]
I got the keys
Two of them, on a ring
I walk from room to room
I'm learning where I'll be
I got the keys

[Outro: doorbell note, a key turning, door closing softly]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 72 BPM, 4/4, B-flat major. Slow, spacious and private, rising to one very large moment.

VOICE: Young female soprano. Verses are breathy and conversational, sung close with small catches in the voice. The chorus is fuller. In the bridge her voice is stacked many times and she belts the top line at full strength. The final chorus drops to a near whisper.

INSTRUMENTS: A doorbell tone that repeats and is taken over by a single piano note in the same rhythm. Solo piano. Soft synth pads. A muted kick and handclaps from the first chorus. A big, reverberant drum kit and sub-bass that arrive only for the bridge. Sounds of a key and a door.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, the doorbell note becoming piano. 0:12 Verse 1. 0:52 Chorus 1. 1:25 Verse 2. 2:05 Chorus 2. 2:38 Bridge, voices stacking, drums crashing in on the third line. 3:05 Final chorus, suddenly quiet, piano and one voice. 3:28 Outro, the doorbell note, a key turning and a door closing at 3:38.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-2020s bedroom-to-arena ballad: intimate and dry at the start, cathedral-sized in the bridge, intimate again at the end.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The bridge at 2:38, when the single voice becomes a crowd of her own voices.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The milestone is a lease, not a licence, and the last chorus changes one line: she is learning where she will be. The song lets the singer be seventeen or forty-five.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Numb achievement, bitterness, a wave of grief, the first step into her own place.
